reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of POINTWISE lies in decomposing basketball possessions into two nested layers: microtransitions (player movement) and macrotransitions (ball events). The microtransition model uses Kalman filtering to estimate player trajectories from optical data, providing high-resolution spatial-temporal inputs. These are then fed into a macrotransition model that predicts discrete events like passes or shots using competing risks hazard models. The expected possession value (EPV) emerges as a scalar reward function derived from the macrotransition chain, which integrates both spatial dynamics and event likelihoods. This duality enables real-time tactical decisions by quantifying the value added or lost by each player’s position and action. Failure modes include sensor noise in tracking data, misclassification of events, and model misspecification of transition probabilities. The system must also account for non-Markovian dependencies in game context, such as momentum shifts or strategic adaptations.
